summary.text: Erin Murphy is a Democratic state senator from St. Paul who represents District 64 and has served as Senate Majority Leader since February 2024; she is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026, against Republican Robert Bushard.
A registered nurse by training, she served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2007 to 2019.

paragraphs.text: Murphy was born in Columbus, Wisconsin, and lives in St. Paul, Minnesota. She earned a B.S. in nursing from the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh in 1984 and an M.A. in organizational leadership from the College of St. Catherine in 2005.
Her career experience includes working as a registered nurse and as the executive director and founder of Our Stories. Our Health.

Murphy represented District 64A in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2007 to 2019, serving as assistant majority leader from 2008 to 2012, majority leader from 2013 to 2014, and deputy minority leader in the 2015 session.
In 2018 she ran in the Democratic primary for governor of Minnesota and received 32 percent of the vote to Tim Walz's 42 percent.
She won the District 64 Senate seat in 2020 and assumed office on January 5, 2021.
Murphy began serving as Senate Majority Leader in February 2024 after Kari Dziedzic stepped down, and her 2025-2026 committee assignments are Rules and Administration, which she chairs, and Finance.
